transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-10-05 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Alex Guerrero (MarlinWorks CTO), Priya Nair (MarlinWorks SRE Lead), Jonah Reed (MarlinWorks Head of Product)

Summary:
Quick intake to understand MarlinWorks' security and compliance constraints for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Focus areas: SOC 2 / ISO expectations, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, RBAC model and least-privilege, audit logs/retention, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), and data residency/retention windows.

Topics covered:
- SOC 2 and ISO requirements and evidence
- SSO integrations (SAML + SCIM) and RBAC mapping
- Audit logging, retention windows, and exportability
- Encryption at rest/in-flight and BYOK KMS options
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for latency, control, and cost

Action items (captured quickly in call): see metadata for owners and due dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Elena: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, we realize you're in the middle of a roadmap sprint so we appreciate it. Quick intros?
[00:12] Alex: Yeah Alex Guerrero, CTO at MarlinWorks. We run the routing and matching stack, SRE and infra are shared across services.
[00:18] Priya: Hi, Priya Nair, SRE lead. I'm focused on security, ops, key management, retention.
[00:22] Jonah: Jonah Reed, head of product, looking at UX impact and latency.
[00:26] Elena: Great. Marcus, want to do a short framing?
[00:29] Marcus: Sure. We'll cover high-level security posture across our Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) options. We'll also call out what evidence we normally provide — SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 summary, pen test report redacted. We want to understand your gating criteria.
[00:44] Alex: For us, the gating is two fold: compliance for enterprise customers (we need SOC 2 and some proof of controls) and the ability to keep certain data in our control — ideally customer PII never leaves our network.
[00:56] Priya: Yep, plus we need SSO with SCIM provisioning and RBAC that lets us enforce least privilege for service accounts. Also audit logs — long term retention for at least 12 months and export to our SIEM.
[01:12] Marcus: Totally makes sense. Quick note: our Hosted plan is fast to get started but customers that require strict data control typically move to Dedicated or Private. We support BYOK with KMS for Dedicated and Private, and Private can be fully customer-managed in a VPC or on-prem.
[01:28] Alex: BYOK meaning we can bring our own customer-managed keys? How involved is that from a networking and ops perspective?
[01:34] Elena: Yes, BYOK is supported in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we have envelope encryption but keys are managed by Redwood; we can discuss a legal arrangement and strict access controls but it isn't typical for Hosted. For Dedicated/Private we integrate with your KMS — we have examples for AWS KMS, GCP KMS and HSMs via KMIP.
[01:49] Priya: KMIP support is important for our HSM vendor. We need to understand the key rotation process and whether Redwood operators ever have access to plaintext.
[01:58] Marcus: Our model for Dedicated/Private is that Redwood operators never see plaintext unless there's an emergency break-glass process — which is logged and audited. Keys are customer-managed for BYOK paths; we can share our runbook.
[02:10] Jonah: What's the typical audit trail look like? We need to map events to our SIEM — is the audit stream JSON?
[02:15] Marcus: Audit logs are available as structured JSON and can be exported to S3 or pushed to your logging endpoint. We include request metadata, token id (redacted), model variant, latency, and decisioning (fallbacks etc). Retention policy is configurable on Dedicated/Private; Hosted has retention tiers we can discuss.
[02:33] Priya: Retention tiers — what's the minimum we can keep logs for and how long can we push out? Our compliance team wants 12 months immutable retention for logs tied to critical flows.
[02:44] Elena: For Hosted we have default retention 90 days for request-level logs, with paid add-ons for longer-term retention. Dedicated includes the ability to store logs in your own S3 bucket with retention you control. Private of course gives you full control.
[02:57] Alex: So if we go Dedicated and push logs to our S3 bucket, we can meet the 12 months requirement?
[03:01] Marcus: Yes — you can control lifecycle policies on your side. We'll also provide a record-of-access audit that shows who from Redwood requested elevated access.
[03:10] Priya: Good. On SSO — we use SAML with Azure AD; SCIM for provisioning would be ideal. Does Redwood support SAML + SCIM out of the box?
[03:20] Elena: Yes. We support SAML for SSO and SCIM for user/group provisioning. For service accounts and API access we recommend a combination of scoped service tokens and RBAC roles that map to your IdP groups.
[03:31] Alex: How fine-grained is RBAC? Can we map internal roles (support, devops, analytics) and restrict, say, tokens from being used to export raw transcripts?
[03:41] Marcus: Our RBAC supports resource-level permissions: models, routes, and datasets. You can create roles that disallow export of raw transcripts or restrict which routes a service token can call. There are also audit hooks for token usage.
[03:52] Priya: Is there a way to require MFA for administrative actions within the Console?
[03:56] Elena: Yes, SAML providers can enforce MFA. We respect the IdP's session policies and also offer two-person approval flows for critical operations in Dedicated/Private — e.g., rotating keys or enabling debugging telemetry.
[04:10] Jonah: On debugging telemetry — if we run production traces for latency debugging, are those traces stored as part of logs? Who has access?
[04:17] Marcus: Traces can be stored with PII redaction options. Access is role gated; we can configure that traces are only accessible to named roles and not to general ops. We also can scrub prompts or store only metadata on request to meet your data retention rules.
[04:32] Alex: Data residency — some of our customers require EU-only processing for EU tenant data. How does Redwood handle region pinning?
[04:39] Elena: We support region pinning on Dedicated and Private. Hosted offers region selection for many models but if you need EU-only for compliance, Dedicated/private is the pattern we use. We also have contractual clauses for data residency in our enterprise agreements.
[04:55] Priya: Pen test evidence — we need to see the last 12 months pen test and vulnerability management cadence, plus your SOC2 auditor name.
[05:04] Marcus: We can provide a SOC 2 Type II summary and redacted pen test report under NDA. We rotate vuln scans monthly and do external pentests quarterly for critical infra. Auditor for our current SOC 2 is Clifton Hunt — I'll confirm the exact firm and add contact details in the packet.
[05:20] Alex: Is there an option for air-gapped on-prem for regulated customers?
[05:25] Elena: Yes, our Private offering can be packaged as an air-gapped on-prem appliance. That tends to be used for highly regulated banks and health orgs; it comes with an extended integration window and additional licensing.
[05:37] Jonah: From a product perspective, how much latency improvement do we see moving from Hosted to Dedicated to Private? We're sensitive to 95th percentile p99 for small requests.
[05:46] Marcus: Generally Dedicated reduces queuing and gives you reserved GPUs so p95/p99 are much tighter. Private can be colocated near your infra to reduce network hop. We can run a micro-benchmark with your traffic profile to show differences — that's one of the next steps.
[06:00] Priya: On compliance for Hosted — you said Hosted stores request logs for 90 days by default; is there a way to opt-out of storing prompts in the clear? We might need to ensure our prompts are never stored unencrypted by a third party.
[06:12] Marcus: For Hosted we anonymize and redact some fields by default, and we offer stricter retention and redaction configs as an add-on. For absolute guarantee that prompts do not leave your control, Dedicated/Private with BYOK is the right path.
[06:28] Alex: What about legal — do we get SOC2 in the contract and SLAs around access and incident response?
[06:34] Elena: Yes, enterprise contracts include SOC2 attestation references and an incident response SLA. We also provide a security addendum covering access controls and data handling.
[06:43] Priya: Patch management cadence? We need to align on maintenance windows and notification lead times.
[06:49] Marcus: For Hosted we do rolling patching with a monthly maintenance window and notify 72 hours ahead for anything non-security. For Dedicated there's a coordination model; if you self-manage nodes in Private, you control the window.
[07:01] Jonah: One last question on exports — if we want to keep transcripts for analytics, can we pull them out in near real-time and then redact before storage?
[07:09] Marcus: Yes. We provide webhook/event hooks for real-time events, and you can configure a pipeline to pull, redact, and then store in your data lake. We also support streaming with field-level redaction.
[07:21] Alex: Ok that covers most of the gating. Let's talk about timeline — our procurement wants a recommended path in 2 weeks. We'll need the SOC documents and a deployment runbook to present to legal and infra.
[07:31] Elena: We'll get the SOC2 summary and pen test memo to you by Friday, and Marcus will share the Private runbook. We'll also propose a benchmark slot for the week of the 11th.
[07:41] Priya: FYI we may bring in procurement and legal on the next call so expect some contract questions.
[07:46] Elena: Noted. Anything else?
[07:48] Jonah: No, thanks.
[07:49] Elena: Great — quick recap, next steps: Elena send SOC and security deck; Marcus send runbook and KMS notes; schedule infra deep-dive. Thanks all.

End of call.
